title: 30-Year Treasury Bond auction (December reopening) — 1:00pm ET, the day after the FOMC decision and the same morning as CPI
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), re-fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes, PDF CreationDate 2026-08-04), FlateDecode streams inflated per page and rows rebuilt from Tm coordinates independently of the proposal that discovered this event. The page-3 row reads verbatim `30-Year BOND / R / Thursday, December 03, 2026 / Thursday, December 10, 2026 / Tuesday, December 15, 2026` — the `R` marks a REOPENING. 1:00pm ET is Treasury's standing coupon-auction convention and is NOT separately sourced. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the confirming primary is the 2026-12-03 coupon announcement. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICALISED 2026-09-09 from `proposals/treasury-30y-bond-2026-12-10.from-treasury-3y-note-2026-12-07.json` (the only proposal for this id), whose date, reopening read and settle date all reproduce against a fresh page-by-page fetch of the same primary. THREE AMENDMENTS to what that proposal carried, all from `api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov` `auctions_query` re-pulled 2026-09-09 (253 rows since 2009-01-01, of which 42 are 30-Year TIPS returned as `security_type: Bond` and excluded on a non-null `ref_cpi_on_issue_date`, leaving 211 nominal). (1) THE EXPECTED SIZE IS $22B, NOT $25B. The proposal names $25B, which is the 30-Year NEW-ISSUE size ($25B at 11 refunding-month new issues, 2024-02-08 through 2026-08-13). A December 30-Year is a REOPENING — 17 of 17 Decembers since 2009 — and the reopening grid is a separate constant: 20 consecutive completed reopenings at exactly $22,000,000,000 from 2024-03-13 through 2026-07-09, with 2026-09-10 already announced at $22B as the 21st. The $22B and $25B streaks run side by side and must never be conflated. (2) THE CUSIP DOES NOT ALREADY EXIST. The proposal reasons that a reopening's security is already outstanding so a when-issued level is quotable well ahead. True in general, false today: the bond being reopened here is the NOVEMBER 2026 new issue, itself unsold until 2026-11-12. The CUSIP exists 28 days before this auction, not now, and this file predicts none. (3) THE FOMC ORDERING IS NOT RARE, THE COMBINATION IS. Stopping the day after an FOMC decision is 4 of 17 Decembers (2011, 2012, 2019, 2025) and 9 of 210 nominal 30-Years since 2009; sharing a session with CPI is 3 of 17 Decembers (2020, 2022, 2023) and 39 of 210 overall. What has NEVER happened is both at once: 0 of 210 nominal 30-Year auctions since 2009 stopped on a CPI release day with an FOMC decision one to five days behind them. CORRIDOR: 26 tracked entries within +/-5 days, three of them high — fomc-2026-12-09 (D-1, confirmed), cpi-2026-12-10 (D+0, confirmed, 08:30 ET, four and a half hours before the auction) and the government-funding deadline / CR expiry 12-11 (D+1), which lands after the CPI print but before the 12-15 settlement. The size decision belonged to the 2026-11-04 quarterly refunding statement; 2026-12-03 merely publishes it. DISCOVERED IN-SWEEP AND PROPOSED IN THIS PR: `treasury-30y-bond-2027-01-13`, the third and final sale of the same bond (announce 2027-01-07, auction Wednesday 2027-01-13, settle 2027-01-15, `R`), which is the leg this event's own stance chains into. Reading it, not trading it: `symbols: []`, the date is `estimate`, and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates-keyed.
